title: Splitting a run while preserving untouched memory
statement: Let a WordRAM program run from configuration $c$ to configuration $c'$ in $n$ steps, with every address touched at each step belonging to a set $K\subseteq\mathbb Z$. For any $k\le n$, there is a configuration $d$ such that the run splits into $k$ steps from $c$ to $d$ and $n-k$ steps from $d$ to $c'$, and $d$'s memory agrees with $c$'s memory at every address outside $K$.
hypotheses_covered: A run of $n$ steps from $c$ to $c'$ whose touched addresses all lie in $K$
